title: Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā
summary: The Perfection of Wisdom in 8,000 lines: in 32 chapters Subhūti, empowered by the Buddha, teaches that the bodhisattva does not apprehend any dharma, not even 'bodhisattva' or 'perfection of wisdom', and so courses in wisdom; all dharmas are like illusions and dreams, even nirvāṇa. It praises the perfection of wisdom as the mother of the buddhas and the book as an object of worship, describes Māra's deeds that obstruct it, the signs of the irreversible bodhisattva, skillful means that keep him from realizing the reality-limit too soon, and ends with the story of Sadāprarudita's search for the teaching from Dharmodgata.

title: Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā
summary: The Perfection of Wisdom in 25,000 lines: the Large Sūtra, expanding the 8,000 with systematic lists — the twenty (or sixteen/eighteen) emptinesses, the 108 samādhis, the dhāraṇī-doors, the stages — and a revised version rearranged to follow the eight topics of the Abhisamayālaṃkāra. It is the sūtra commented on in the Chinese Dazhidu lun and the Abhisamayālaṃkāra tradition.

title: Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā
summary: The Diamond Sūtra: in dialogue with Subhūti the Buddha teaches that the bodhisattva leads all beings to nirvāṇa while no being is led, gives without being supported by any thing, sees the Tathāgata in no-marks, treats the dharma like a raft, and should produce a mind supported nowhere. Its dialectic 'what is taught as A is not-A; therefore it is called A' runs throughout; it ends with the verse on conditioned things as stars, a fault of vision, a lamp, an illusion, dew, a bubble, a dream, lightning and a cloud.

title: Prajñāpāramitāhṛdaya
summary: The Heart Sūtra: Avalokiteśvara, coursing in the deep perfection of wisdom, sees the five aggregates empty of own-being; form is emptiness and emptiness is form; all dharmas are marked by emptiness, unborn and unceasing; in emptiness there are no aggregates, elements, links, truths, knowledge or attainment; relying on the perfection of wisdom bodhisattvas are without obstruction and buddhas awaken; it ends with the mantra gate gate pāragate pārasaṃgate bodhi svāhā. Short (without frame) and long (with frame) versions exist.

title: Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra
summary: The Lotus Sūtra: the Buddha reveals that the three vehicles were skillful means and there is only the one buddha-vehicle; all who hear it, even with a single flower or a child's drawing of a stūpa, will become buddhas; the śrāvakas receive predictions of buddhahood. Through the parables of the burning house, the prodigal son, the medicinal herbs, the conjured city, the jewel in the robe and the physician's sons it teaches skillful means; the stūpa of the past buddha Prabhūtaratna appears; the nāga princess becomes a buddha instantly; bodhisattvas rise from the earth; the Buddha reveals that he awakened incalculable aeons ago and his lifespan is immeasurable; it praises the dharma-preacher, Sadāparibhūta, Bhaiṣajyarāja's self-offering, Avalokiteśvara's rescue and Samantabhadra's protection.

title: Wuliangyi jing (Sūtra of Innumerable Meanings)

title: Karuṇāpuṇḍarīka-sūtra

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)

title: Gaṇḍavyūha-sūtra
summary: The final part of the Avataṃsaka, also an independent sūtra: sent by Mañjuśrī, the youth Sudhana visits fifty-odd spiritual friends — monks, laymen and laywomen, a courtesan, kings, goddesses of the night, a boy teacher, the Buddha's mother Māyā and wife Gopā — each teaching one liberation; Maitreya shows him the tower of Vairocana in which all worlds are reflected; he returns to Mañjuśrī and finally merges with Samantabhadra, whose vows (the Bhadracarī) conclude the text.

title: Daśabhūmika-sūtra
summary: The Sūtra of the Ten Grounds, spoken by the bodhisattva Vajragarbha: the ten stages (bhūmi) of the bodhisattva from Joyful (pramuditā) to Cloud of Dharma (dharmameghā), each with its perfection, purifications and attainments; in the sixth ground the three realms are 'mind only' and the twelve links depend on mind; at the eighth, Immovable, the bodhisattva attains the acceptance of non-arising and is roused by the buddhas not to enter peace.

title: Bhadracarīpraṇidhāna

title: Laṅkāvatāra-sūtra

title: Vimalakīrtinirdeśa
summary: The layman Vimalakīrti of Vaiśālī, a bodhisattva of inconceivable skillful means, feigns illness; the Buddha's disciples decline to visit him, recalling how he had corrected them; Mañjuśrī goes, and in Vimalakīrti's empty room they discuss the bodhisattva's illness born of compassion, inconceivable liberation (Sumeru in a mustard seed), a goddess who turns Śāriputra into a woman, the passions as the family of the Tathāgata, and the entrance into non-duality, which Vimalakīrti shows by silence. The purity of the buddha-field follows the purity of the mind.

notes: Locator: Sanskrit chapter.paragraph (vkn c|p), Kumārajīva's chapter in teaching sections. The brief's 'ch. 9' for the silence is Kumārajīva's numbering (= Skt ch. 8).

title: Saṃdhinirmocana-sūtra
summary: The 'Sūtra Unravelling the Intent': the ultimate is inexpressible, non-dual, beyond identity and difference and of one taste; the ādāna- or ālaya-vijñāna holding all seeds; the three characteristics (imagined, dependent, perfected) and three naturelessnesses as the Buddha's intent behind 'all dharmas lack own-being'; the three turnings of the dharma-wheel of which the third, 'well-distinguished', is definitive; calm abiding and insight and 'the image is cognition only'; the perfections and grounds; the bodies of the Tathāgata.
alt_titles: Jie shenmi jing 解深密經 (T676, Xuanzang 647)

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana) (Tibetan: the third turning of the wheel)
attribution.scholarly: Anonymous; layered composition c. 2nd-4th c.; quoted whole in the Yogācārabhūmi

structure.description: 10 chapters in Tibetan (Lamotte's ed.): 1 introduction; 2-4 the ultimate (Gambhīrārthasaṃdhinirmocana, Suviśuddhamati, Subhūti); 5 mind (Viśālamati); 6 the characteristics (Guṇākara); 7 naturelessness (Paramārthasamudgata); 8 yoga (Maitreya); 9 perfections and grounds (Avalokiteśvara); 10 the Tathāgata's activity (Mañjuśrī). Xuanzang's version has 8 chapters (2-4 joined)

notes: No Sanskrit survives (fragments quoted); Chinese T676 (vol. 16) not local; Tibetan D106 present in sources_raw/derge-kangyur (catalog:Derge-Kangyur:D106) but not read in this phase. Chapter-level refs, Lamotte/Tibetan numbering.

title: Śūraṅgamasamādhi-sūtra
summary: The sūtra of the 'heroic-going' concentration, which only bodhisattvas of the tenth ground attain and which contains all other samādhis; it tells of Māra's conversion and predictions, of Mañjuśrī's past lives as a pratyekabuddha and a buddha, and of bodhisattvas who display nirvāṇa without abandoning beings.
alt_titles: Shoulengyan sanmei jing 首楞嚴三昧經 (T642, Kumārajīva 402-409)

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)
attribution.scholarly: Anonymous; Lokakṣema's lost Chinese (2nd c.) shows an early date

notes: Distinct from the Chinese Śūraṅgama Sūtra (src:surangama-sutra).

title: Śūraṅgama-sūtra (Chinese Shoulengyan jing, T945)
summary: A ten-fascicle sūtra transmitted in China: after Ānanda is nearly seduced through a spell, the Buddha shows that the mind is not located in seven places and that the true, perceiving nature (the 'wondrous bright true mind', the tathāgatagarbha) neither comes nor goes; twenty-five sages describe their perfect penetrations, and Mañjuśrī selects Avalokiteśvara's turning of hearing back to hear the self-nature as best for this world; the four clear instructions on purity (no sex, killing, stealing, false claims), the Śūraṅgama mantra and altar, the stages of the path, the destinies, and the fifty demonic states arising from the five aggregates in meditation.
alt_titles: Da foding rulai miyin xiuzheng liaoyi zhu pusa wanxing shoulengyan jing 大佛頂如來密因修證了義諸菩薩萬行首楞嚴經
Tibetan partial translation from Chinese (Toh 236, ch. 10)

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana); tradition: brought to China by the Indian monk Pāramiti (Pramiti) and translated at Guangzhou in 705, with the court official Fang Rong as scribe
attribution.scholarly: Many modern scholars hold it was composed in China c. early 8th c.; its Indian origin has been questioned since the 8th c. in Japan and argued against by 20th-c. scholars; defended by the Chan and later Chinese tradition

notes: T945 (vol. 19) is not in the local CBETA subset; fascicle-level refs from memory. The Tibetan Toh 236 (a translation from Chinese of part of the last chapter) is attested in the local Derge catalogue.

title: Samādhirāja-sūtra
summary: The 'King of Samādhis' (also Candrapradīpa): the Buddha teaches the young Candraprabha the samādhi of the sameness of the nature of all dharmas, in verses that liken all dharmas to dreams, magical displays, the moon in water and mirages, reject 'is' and 'is not' as extremes, and praise recollection of the Buddha, patience and renunciation; Candraprabha's past life as the monk who gave up his life to preserve the dharma. Much quoted by Candrakīrti and by Gampopa for Mahāmudrā.
alt_titles: Yuedeng sanmei jing 月燈三昧經 (T639, Narendrayaśas 557)

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)

title: Sukhāvatīvyūha-sūtra (larger)
summary: The Larger Sūtra of Immeasurable Life: the monk Dharmākara, before the buddha Lokeśvararāja, makes forty-eight vows (Chinese T360; the Sanskrit has a different count) to create a pure land, and after aeons of practice becomes the buddha Amitābha / Amitāyus in Sukhāvatī to the west; the eighteenth vow promises birth there to all who with sincere faith wish to be born there and call him to mind even ten times, excepting those who committed the five grave offences or slandered the dharma; it describes the land, the three grades of aspirants and the vulnerability of beings in this world.
alt_titles: Wuliangshou jing 無量壽經 (T360, attributed to Saṃghavarman 252)

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana) on the Vulture Peak to Ānanda and Maitreya
attribution.scholarly: Anonymous, c. 1st-2nd c. CE (Gandhāra?); the T360 attribution to Saṃghavarman (252) is doubted, many scholars assign it to Buddhabhadra and Baoyun (421)

scholarly.text: c. 100-200 CE; earliest Chinese versions 2nd-3rd c.

notes: Doctrine and lineages of Pure Land belong to U43; this unit owns the sūtra entry. 18th vow read locally in T360 (268a26-27).

title: Sukhāvatīvyūha-sūtra (smaller)
summary: The Smaller Sūtra (Amituo jing): the Buddha, unasked, describes Sukhāvatī to Śāriputra — its jewelled trees, lotus ponds and birds that sing the dharma; beings cannot be born there by few roots of merit, but whoever holds fast to the name of Amitābha for one to seven days with an undistracted mind will see him appear at death and be born there; the buddhas of the six directions confirm it.
alt_titles: Amituo jing 阿彌陀經 (T366, Kumārajīva 402)
Chengzan jingtu fo sheshou jing (T367, Xuanzang)

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana) at Śrāvastī

notes: Holding the name passage read locally in T366 (347b10-13).

title: Amitāyurdhyāna-sūtra (Guan wuliangshou jing)
summary: The Contemplation Sūtra: Queen Vaidehī, imprisoned by her son Ajātaśatru, asks for a world without sorrow; the Buddha shows her the pure lands and teaches sixteen contemplations — the setting sun, water, the ground, the trees, ponds, towers, the lotus throne, the images, Amitābha's body, Avalokiteśvara, Mahāsthāmaprāpta, one's own birth there, and the three grades each of upper, middle and lower birth (nine grades); even the lowest evil-doer who at death calls 'namo Amitābha Buddha' ten times is born in a lotus there.
alt_titles: Guan wuliangshou fo jing 觀無量壽佛經 (T365, attributed to Kālayaśas 424-442)

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana) at Rājagṛha, to Vaidehī
attribution.scholarly: No Sanskrit or Tibetan version; many scholars hold it was composed in Central Asia or China in the 5th c.

structure.description: sixteen contemplations; the last three give the nine grades of birth

notes: Lower-lower grade read locally in T365 (346a12-26).

title: Pratyutpannabuddhasaṃmukhāvasthitasamādhi-sūtra
summary: The sūtra of the samādhi in which the buddhas of the present stand before one: by recollecting Amitābha single-mindedly for seven days and nights the practitioner sees him (and all buddhas) face to face, as in a dream; the buddhas seen are understood as made by mind, neither coming nor going. One of the earliest Mahāyāna sūtras in Chinese.
alt_titles: Banzhou sanmei jing 般舟三昧經 (T417-418, Lokakṣema 179)
da ltar gyi sangs rgyas mngon sum du bzhugs pa'i ting nge 'dzin (Toh 133)

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana) to the lay bodhisattva Bhadrapāla

notes: T417/T418 (vol. 13) not local; chapter-level refs from memory.

title: Akṣobhyavyūha
summary: The array of the buddha Akṣobhya and his eastern land Abhirati, the vows he made as a monk never to feel anger; birth in his land is an early pure-land aspiration; Vimalakīrti's home land.
alt_titles: Achu foguo jing 阿閦佛國經 (T313, Lokakṣema)

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)

title: Bhaiṣajyaguru-sūtra
summary: The sūtra of the Medicine Buddha, Bhaiṣajyaguru Vaiḍūryaprabha, whose eastern land is of lapis; his twelve great vows to heal bodily and mental ills, provide for the poor and free beings from wrong views; hearing and keeping his name prevents evil rebirth; rites of lamps, banners and recitation to prolong the life of the sick and dying.
alt_titles: Yaoshi liuliguang rulai benyuan gongde jing 藥師琉璃光如來本願功德經 (T450, Xuanzang 650)

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana) to Mañjuśrī at Vaiśālī
attribution.scholarly: Anonymous; Gilgit ms (6th-7th c.); Chinese 5th-8th c.

editions.name: ed. P. L. Vaidya 1961 (after Dutt's Gilgit ed.)

title: Kāraṇḍavyūha-sūtra
summary: The 'Basket Array': the compassion and saving deeds of Avalokiteśvara, who descends into the hells and the realms of hungry ghosts, and whose body contains worlds in its pores; it first reveals the six-syllable great vidyā oṃ maṇipadme hūṃ as his heart, obtained with difficulty and bestowing liberation.

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)

title: Kṣitigarbha Pūrvapraṇidhāna Sūtra (Dizang pusa benyuan jing)
summary: The sūtra of Kṣitigarbha's past vows, spoken in the Trāyastriṃśa heaven: in past lives as a brahmin girl and as a king he vowed to save beings from the hells and not to become a buddha until the hells are empty; it describes the hells, the merit of offerings for the dead during the forty-nine days, and the benefits of reciting his name.
alt_titles: 地藏菩薩本願經 (T412, attributed to Śikṣānanda)

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)
attribution.scholarly: No Indic or Tibetan version; widely held a Chinese composition (Tang or later)

title: Daśacakra-Kṣitigarbha-sūtra
summary: The 'Ten Wheels' sūtra of Kṣitigarbha (in the Mahāsaṃnipāta): Kṣitigarbha's powers and a king's ten wheels of rule; warnings against those who revile monks of the three vehicles; a text of the Chinese Three Stages school.
alt_titles: Dasheng daji dizang shilun jing (T411, Xuanzang 651)

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)

title: Mahāratnakūṭa (collection)
summary: The 'Great Heap of Jewels', a collection of forty-nine Mahāyāna sūtras (Chinese T310, compiled by Bodhiruci 706-713; Tibetan Toh 45-93), including the Kāśyapaparivarta, Akṣobhyavyūha, Amitābhavyūha, Śrīmālā, Ugra and Bodhisattvapiṭaka.
alt_titles: Da baoji jing 大寶積經 (T310)

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)
attribution.scholarly: A collection assembled in China/Tibet from earlier sūtras

title: Kāśyapaparivarta
summary: The chapter of Kāśyapa (the 'Ratnakūṭa' proper): sets of four qualities that make or break a bodhisattva; the middle way as the true examination of dharmas — 'is' and 'is not', permanent and impermanent, self and no-self are two extremes; emptiness does not make dharmas empty, they are empty; better a view of self as large as Mount Sumeru than a view of emptiness, which is incurable, like a medicine that stays in the belly; the lamp that dispels darkness of a thousand years.
alt_titles: Yiri monibao jing 遺日摩尼寶經 (T350, Lokakṣema)

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)

notes: Locator: § numbers; §§56-71 read locally.

title: Akṣayamatinirdeśa-sūtra
summary: The teaching of the bodhisattva Akṣayamati on eighty 'inexhaustible' qualities of the bodhisattva; it defines sūtras of definitive meaning (nītārtha) as those teaching emptiness, signlessness, no self, no being, and sūtras of provisional meaning (neyārtha) as those teaching self, being, person and the like, and gives the four reliances (on the dharma not the person, meaning not letter, definitive not provisional, gnosis not consciousness).
alt_titles: Wujinyi pusa jing (T397.12, in the Mahāsaṃnipāta)
blo gros mi zad pas bstan pa (Toh 175)

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)

notes: Sanskrit lost apart from citations (Prasannapadā, Śikṣāsamuccaya); chapter-level refs.

title: Ugraparipṛcchā
summary: The Inquiry of the householder Ugra: the lay and monastic bodhisattva's conduct; the householder should see his household as a burning house and practice the perfections; praises the forest life for the renunciant bodhisattva.

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)

notes: T322/T323 in local CBETA T12.

title: Rāṣṭrapālaparipṛcchā
summary: The Inquiry of Rāṣṭrapāla: the bodhisattva's forest austerity and a sharp prophecy of corrupt future monks.

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)

title: Bodhisattvapiṭaka-sūtra
summary: A long Ratnakūṭa sūtra on the bodhisattva's discipline and the six perfections; much cited in the Śikṣāsamuccaya.

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)

title: Upāyakauśalya-sūtra
summary: The Sūtra on Skillful Means: how the bodhisattva's apparently wrong acts are done out of skillful means and compassion — including the story of the Buddha in a past life killing a man who was about to murder five hundred merchants, to save both.

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)

notes: T345/T346 are in local CBETA T12.

title: Pitāputrasamāgama-sūtra
summary: The meeting of the father (the Buddha) and son (Śuddhodana); on emptiness and the elements; frequently cited by Madhyamaka authors.

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)

title: Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra
summary: The Sūtra of Golden Light: the Buddha's lifespan is immeasurable; the confession chapter (born from a golden drum seen in a dream); emptiness; the four great kings, Sarasvatī, Śrī and the earth goddess vow to protect lands where it is honored; a treatise on righteous kingship; the prince who gave his body to a starving tigress. Central to state-protection rites in East Asia and to Tibetan and Newar practice.

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)
attribution.scholarly: Anonymous, grew in layers c. 4th-8th c.

scholarly.text: c. 4th c. (Dharmakṣema's Chinese early 5th c.); expanded to 8th c.

title: Lalitavistara
summary: The 'Extensive Play': the life of the Buddha from Tuṣita to the first sermon, told as the display of a being already awakened; originally a Sarvāstivāda biography reworked as a Mahāyāna vaipulya sūtra.

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)

title: Tathāgatācintyaguhyanirdeśa
summary: The secrets of the Tathāgata's body, speech and mind, taught by Vajrapāṇi; one of Nepal's nine dharmas.

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)

title: Ratnamegha-sūtra
summary: The 'Cloud of Jewels': on the bodhisattva's qualities and discipline, much cited in the Śikṣāsamuccaya.

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)

title: Dharmasaṃgīti-sūtra
summary: The 'Recitation of the Dharma': a collection of bodhisattvas' statements on the dharma, much cited by Śāntideva and Kamalaśīla.

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)

notes: Tibetan Toh 238 confirmed in the local catalogue; Chinese version not identified here (gap).

title: Sāgaramatiparipṛcchā
summary: The Inquiry of Sāgaramati, part of the Mahāsaṃnipāta; the Ratnagotravibhāga draws on it for the bodhisattva's deliberate rebirth and the simile of the beryl stone in mud.

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)

title: Brahmaviśeṣacintiparipṛcchā
summary: The Inquiry of the Brahmā Viśeṣacinti, on the sameness of all dharmas and the non-arising of dharmas.

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)

title: Ajātaśatrukaukṛtyavinodana
summary: The dispelling of king Ajātaśatru's remorse for killing his father: Mañjuśrī shows that the karmic obstruction is empty and the king obtains the acceptance of dharmas.

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)

title: Gaganagañjaparipṛcchā
summary: The Inquiry of Gaganagañja (in the Mahāsaṃnipāta); cited in the Ratnagotravibhāga for the simile of space, wind and water for the mind's nature and the defilements.

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)

title: Śālistamba-sūtra
summary: The 'Rice Seedling' sūtra, taught by Maitreya to Śāriputra: 'whoever sees dependent origination sees the dharma, whoever sees the dharma sees the Buddha'; the twelve links explained outwardly by the seed and sprout, inwardly by the six elements, as neither eternal nor annihilated.

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana); spoken by Maitreya

title: Anavataptanāgarājaparipṛcchā
summary: The Inquiry of the nāga king Anavatapta, source of the verse cited by Candrakīrti: 'what is born from conditions is unborn; it has no birth by nature; what depends on conditions is called empty; who knows emptiness is heedful'.

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)

title: Saṃvṛtiparamārthasatyanirdeśa
summary: The teaching on the conventional and ultimate truths, spoken to Mañjuśrī: the ultimate is beyond all expression, even that of the Buddha.

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)

title: Bhadrakalpika-sūtra
summary: The sūtra of the Fortunate Aeon, naming the thousand buddhas of this aeon, of whom Śākyamuni is the fourth and Maitreya the fifth.

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)

title: Mahāsaṃnipāta (collection)
summary: The 'Great Assembly' collection (Chinese T397, 60 fascicles), including the Akṣayamatinirdeśa, Ratnaketu, Gaganagañja and the Candragarbha with its prophecy of the decline of the dharma.

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)
attribution.scholarly: A Chinese assemblage (5th-6th c.) of Indian and Central Asian sūtras

title: Ākāśagarbha-sūtra
summary: The sūtra of the bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha, which lists the root downfalls of kings, ministers and beginner bodhisattvas and teaches confession before Ākāśagarbha, who appears in dreams; source (via the Śikṣāsamuccaya) of the Tibetan list of eighteen root bodhisattva downfalls.

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)

title: Triskandhaka (Sūtra of the Three Heaps)
summary: The confession before the thirty-five buddhas, rejoicing and dedication — the 'three heaps' of practice; recited daily in Tibetan practice with prostrations; its liturgy is contained in the Upāliparipṛcchā.

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)

title: Vinayaviniścaya-Upāliparipṛcchā
summary: The Inquiry of Upāli on the bodhisattva's discipline: faults of bodhisattvas differ from those of śrāvakas; confession before the thirty-five buddhas.

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)

title: Bodhisattvaprātimokṣa-sūtra
summary: A short manual of the bodhisattva's vow ceremony and offences, related to the Bodhisattvabhūmi's chapter on discipline.

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)

title: Fanwang jing (Brahmā's Net Sūtra, Mahāyāna)
summary: The East Asian bodhisattva-precept scripture: the ten major and forty-eight minor precepts (no killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, selling alcohol, speaking of others' faults, praising self and disparaging others, stinginess, anger, reviling the three jewels; and minor rules including not eating meat or the five pungent plants); the buddha-nature precepts binding lay and ordained alike.

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana) by Vairocana on the lotus-throne

notes: Distinct from the Pali Brahmajāla Sutta (src:brahmajala-sutta, DN 1).

title: Upāsakaśīla-sūtra
summary: The sūtra of the lay bodhisattva precepts (Chinese T1488, Dharmakṣema 426): the lay bodhisattva's six major and twenty-eight minor precepts.

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)

title: Maitreyavyākaraṇa
summary: The prophecy of Maitreya: his future birth in Ketumatī, awakening under the dragon-flower tree and three assemblies.

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)

title: Nīlakaṇṭha Dhāraṇī Sūtra (Great Compassion Dhāraṇī)
summary: The sūtra of the thousand-armed, thousand-eyed Avalokiteśvara's Great Compassion Dhāraṇī (Dabei zhou): its recitation removes karmic hindrances; the bodhisattva's vows; recited daily in Chinese, Korean, Japanese and Vietnamese monasteries.
alt_titles: Qianshou qianyan guanshiyin pusa guangda yuanman wuai dabeixin tuoluoni jing (T1060, Bhagavaddharma, 7th c.)

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana) (spoken by Avalokiteśvara)

title: Uṣṇīṣavijayā Dhāraṇī Sūtra
summary: The Victorious Uṣṇīṣa dhāraṇī given to the deva Supratiṣṭhita, destined for evil rebirths, which purifies all evil destinies; inscribed on pillars across Tang China.

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)

title: Tathāgatagarbha-sūtra
summary: The Buddha displays countless lotuses whose closing petals reveal buddhas seated within, and explains: all beings, though in the midst of defilements, have within them the Tathāgata's knowledge, eyes and body, seated in meditation, unmoving — the tathāgatagarbha. Nine similes: a buddha in a withered lotus, honey amid bees, a kernel in its husk, gold in filth, a treasure beneath a poor man's house, a seed within a fruit, a golden image wrapped in rags, a future king in the womb of a destitute woman, a golden statue inside a clay mould.
alt_titles: Dafangdeng rulaizang jing 大方等如來藏經 (T666, Buddhabhadra c. 420)
de bzhin gshegs pa'i snying po (Toh 258)

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana) at Rājagṛha, in the Vulture Peak's jewel-pavilion
attribution.scholarly: Anonymous; perhaps the earliest tathāgatagarbha text, c. 3rd c. CE (Chinese c. 290-306, lost; extant 420)

notes: Sanskrit lost apart from RGV citations; T666 (vol. 16) not local; Tibetan D258 in the local catalogue.

title: Śrīmālādevīsiṃhanāda-sūtra
summary: Queen Śrīmālā, with the Buddha's approval, roars the lion's roar: her ten vows and three great aspirations; embracing the true dharma; the one vehicle into which the three vehicles merge; the arhat's nirvāṇa is not final; the tathāgatagarbha is the dharmakāya obscured by defilements; the two kinds of emptiness-knowledge of the garbha (empty of defilements, not empty of buddha-qualities); the dharmakāya's perfections of permanence, bliss, self and purity; saṃsāra and nirvāṇa depend on the garbha; the innately pure mind defiled is hard to understand.
alt_titles: Shengman shizihou yisheng da fangbian fangguang jing 勝鬘師子吼一乘大方便方廣經 (T353, Guṇabhadra 436)
lha mo dpal phreng gi seng ge'i sgra (Toh 92)

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana); spoken by Queen Śrīmālā of Ayodhyā, daughter of Prasenajit, with the Buddha's confirmation

structure.description: 15 chapters in T353: 1 true qualities of the Tathāgata; 2 ten vows; 3 three aspirations; 4 embracing (the true dharma); 5 one vehicle; 6 the unlimited noble truths; 7 tathāgatagarbha; 8 dharmakāya; 9 the hidden truth of emptiness; 10 one truth; 11 one refuge; 12 inversion and truth; 13 self-nature purity; 14 true children; 15 Śrīmālā

notes: Chapter list and key lines (221c16, 222a23, 222b05, 222b28) read locally in T353.

title: Anūnatvāpūrṇatvanirdeśa
summary: The teaching of 'neither decrease nor increase': the realm of beings neither decreases nor increases; the sattvadhātu is the tathāgatagarbha, the tathāgatagarbha is the dharmakāya; the dharmadhātu has three aspects — endowed from beginningless time with inseparable pure qualities, covered by separable defilements, and equal to the end of time.
alt_titles: Buzeng bujian jing 不增不減經 (T668, Bodhiruci 525)

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana) to Śāriputra
attribution.scholarly: Anonymous; extant only in Chinese and RGV quotations

title: Mahāyāna Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra
summary: The Buddha's final Mahāyāna teaching on the day of his parinirvāṇa: the Tathāgata is permanent and unchanging; his parinirvāṇa is a skillful display; nirvāṇa has permanence, bliss, self and purity; 'self' means the tathāgatagarbha; all sentient beings have buddha-nature, obscured by defilements; buddha-nature is the emptiness of the highest meaning, wisdom, the middle way. The early part (Faxian's 6-fascicle version) excludes the icchantika; the later part (Dharmakṣema's 40-fascicle version, Lion's Roar and Kāśyapa chapters) affirms that icchantikas too have buddha-nature. It forbids eating meat.

T375 (36 juan, 'southern text', revised by Huiyan and Xie Lingyun)
Da banniyuan jing 大般泥洹經 (T376, Faxian & Buddhabhadra 418, 6 juan)
yongs su mya ngan las 'das pa chen po (Toh 119 from Sanskrit; Toh 120 from Chinese)

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana) at Kuśinagara on the day of his parinirvāṇa
attribution.scholarly: Anonymous; the core (≈ T376) c. 2nd-3rd c.; the additional chapters of T374 from Dharmakṣema's further manuscripts (Central Asia), 5th c.

tradition.text: the last day of the Buddha's life

scholarly.text: core c. 200-300 CE; expanded to c. 400; Chinese 418 and 421

structure.description: T374: 40 juan, 13 chapters (壽命品 ... 如來性品 ... 聖行 ... 梵行 ... 光明遍照高貴德王菩薩品 ... 師子吼菩薩品 ... 迦葉菩薩品 ... 憍陳如品)

notes: Locator: juan (fascicle) of T374; Taishō lines in teaching sections (read locally). Not to be confused with the Pali Mahāparinibbāna Sutta (src:mahaparinibbana-sutta).

title: Aṅgulimālīya-sūtra
summary: The Mahāyāna retelling of the converted murderer Aṅgulimāla, who teaches famous disciples that the tathāgatagarbha is the permanent self; it criticizes a nihilistic reading of emptiness and forbids meat.
alt_titles: Yangjuemoluo jing 央掘魔羅經 (T120, Guṇabhadra)
sor mo'i phreng ba la phan pa (Toh 213)

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)

title: Mahābherīhārakaparivarta
summary: The 'Great Drum' sūtra: the permanence of the Tathāgata and of nirvāṇa and the one vehicle, proclaimed like a great drum; it prophesies a future preacher of the teaching.
alt_titles: Dafagu jing 大法鼓經 (T270, Guṇabhadra)
rnga bo che chen po'i le'u (Toh 222)

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)

title: Mahāmegha-sūtra
summary: The 'Great Cloud' sūtra, affirming the Tathāgata's permanence and the tathāgatagarbha; its prophecy of a female ruler was used in China under Empress Wu.
alt_titles: Dafangdeng wuxiang jing 大方等無想經 (T387, Dharmakṣema)

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)

notes: T387/T388 present in local CBETA T12.

title: Jñānālokālaṃkāra-sūtra
summary: The 'Ornament of the Light of Knowledge' (Sarvabuddhaviṣayāvatāra): the Tathāgata is unborn and unceasing; similes of the buddha's activity cited in RGV chapter 4.
alt_titles: Rulai zhuangyan zhihui guangming ru yiqie fo jingjie jing (T357)

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)

title: Dhāraṇīśvararāja-paripṛcchā (Tathāgatamahākaruṇānirdeśa)
summary: The Inquiry of Dhāraṇīśvararāja, on the Tathāgata's great compassion and the purification of the gotra like the cleaning of a beryl; the Ratnagotravibhāga's framework of the seven vajra points draws on it.
alt_titles: Dafangdeng daji jing, Tuoluonizizaiwang pusa pin (T397.1)

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)

notes: Tibetan Toh number not verified locally (gap).

title: Ratnagotravibhāga (Mahāyānottaratantraśāstra)
summary: The treatise on the jewel-lineage: seven vajra points — Buddha, dharma, saṅgha, the element (dhātu, the tathāgatagarbha), awakening, qualities, activity; all beings are tathāgatagarbhas for three reasons; the element explained by ten aspects and by nine similes of the buddha within the sheaths of defilement; the four perfections of the dharmakāya; the element empty of adventitious stains and not empty of the inseparable qualities; why buddha-nature was taught (five faults); awakening as transformation of the basis; the sixty-four qualities; unceasing, effortless activity like Indra's reflection, the drum, clouds, Brahmā, the sun, the wish-gem, echo, space and earth.
alt_titles: Jiujing yisheng baoxing lun 究竟一乘寶性論 (T1611, Ratnamati 511)
theg pa chen po rgyud bla ma'i bstan bcos (Toh 4024)

attribution.tradition: Tibetan tradition: the verses taught by Maitreya to Asaṅga (one of the five Maitreya treatises), the commentary by Asaṅga; Chinese tradition (Fazang and others): composed by Sāramati (Jianhui)
attribution.scholarly: Anonymous or of uncertain authorship; core verses c. 4th-5th c.; the Sāramati attribution is Chinese, the Maitreya/Asaṅga attribution Tibetan (from the 11th c. rediscovery by Maitrīpa)

structure.description: 5 chapters (Johnston): 1 the tathāgatagarbha (with the three jewels), 2 awakening, 3 qualities, 4 activity, 5 benefits; verses with prose commentary

notes: Chapter colophons and cited verses read in the local e-text (Johnston numbering; Takasaki's numbering differs slightly in chapter 1). Registry lists src:ratnagotravibhaga; U41 (five Maitreya texts) may also contribute.

title: Ratnagotravibhāgavyākhyā
summary: The prose commentary that accompanies the verses of the Ratnagotravibhāga, quoting the Tathāgatagarbha Sūtra, Śrīmālā, Anūnatvāpūrṇatvanirdeśa, Dhāraṇīśvararāja and other sūtras.
alt_titles: theg pa chen po rgyud bla ma'i bstan bcos rnam par bshad pa (Toh 4025)

attribution.tradition: Asaṅga (Tibetan)
attribution.scholarly: Uncertain; transmitted with the verses in Sanskrit and Chinese

title: Foxing lun (Treatise on Buddha-Nature)
summary: A treatise in Chinese (T1610) attributed to Vasubandhu and translated by Paramārtha: buddha-nature as the suchness revealed by the two emptinesses; three kinds of buddha-nature (abiding, emerging, attained); refutes the view that some beings lack it.

attribution.tradition: Vasubandhu, tr. Paramārtha
attribution.scholarly: Probably compiled or substantially reworked by Paramārtha in China, 6th c.

title: Dasheng qixin lun (Awakening of Faith in the Mahāyāna)
summary: The 'Awakening of Faith': the one mind has two aspects — mind as suchness and mind as arising and ceasing; the tathāgatagarbha and the ālayavijñāna; original awakening (benjue), non-awakening and actualized awakening; suchness as empty and not empty; five practices and calm-insight; recollection of Amitābha for the timid. The most influential buddha-nature treatise in East Asia.
alt_titles: 大乘起信論 (T1666, attributed to Paramārtha 550; T1667, Śikṣānanda)

attribution.tradition: Aśvaghoṣa, translated by Paramārtha
attribution.scholarly: No Indic original; widely held to have been composed in China in the mid-6th c.; the attribution was already questioned in the Sui dynasty

notes: Its Huayan and Korean commentaries (Fazang, Wonhyo) belong to U54/U55.

title: Vajrasamādhi-sūtra (Jingang sanmei jing)
summary: A sūtra on the 'adamantine absorption' combining tathāgatagarbha, emptiness and Chan contemplation, including 'guarding the one' and the 'original enlightenment'; commented on by Wonhyo.

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)
attribution.scholarly: Composed in Korea c. 685 (R. Buswell's thesis) or China, late 7th c.

title: Yuanjue jing (Sūtra of Perfect Enlightenment)
summary: Twelve bodhisattvas question the Buddha on perfect enlightenment, the original mind of all beings; ignorance is like flowers seen in the sky by diseased eyes; the three contemplations of stillness (śamatha), illusion (samāpatti) and dhyāna; central to Zongmi and to Korean Seon curricula.
alt_titles: Dafangguang yuanjue xiuduoluo liaoyi jing 圓覺經 (T842, attributed to Buddhatrāta)

attribution.tradition: Spoken by the Buddha Śākyamuni (tradition's account: buddhavacana)

title: Theg pa chen po rgyud bla ma'i ṭīkā (Gyaltsab Je's commentary on the Uttaratantra)
summary: Gyaltsab Darma Rinchen's commentary on the Ratnagotravibhāga (the 'Dar ṭīk'), reading the buddha-element as the emptiness of the mind — the naturally abiding lineage — in the manner of Tsongkhapa's Madhyamaka.

attribution.tradition: Gyaltsab Je

title: Rgyud bla ma'i 'grel bshad de kho na nyid rab tu gsal ba'i me long (Gö Lotsawa)
summary: Gö Lotsawa Zhönnu Pel's commentary on the Ratnagotravibhāga, relating buddha-nature to Mahāmudrā and the sūtra-based Mahāmudrā of Gampopa.

attribution.tradition: Gö Lotsawa

title: De bzhin gshegs pa'i snying po bstan pa (Rangjung Dorje's Treatise on Buddha-Nature)
summary: The Third Karmapa's short verse treatise on buddha-nature: the ground is mind's nature, luminous and empty, obscured by adventitious stains; purification is Mahāmudrā.

attribution.tradition: Karmapa Rangjung Dorje

title: Rgyud bla ma'i 'grel pa phyir mi ldog pa seng ge'i nga ro (Jamgön Kongtrul)
summary: Jamgön Kongtrul's commentary on the Ratnagotravibhāga ('The Unassailable Lion's Roar'), presenting it as a text of the definitive third turning in a shentong-leaning reading.

attribution.tradition: Jamgön Kongtrul

title: Bde gshegs snying po'i stong thun chen mo seng ge'i nga ro (Mipham)
summary: Mipham's 'Lion's Roar' exposition of buddha-nature, arguing that the tathāgatagarbha is the union of luminosity and emptiness and that the buddha-qualities are primordially present, avoiding both a merely negative emptiness and an existent self.

attribution.tradition: Ju Mipham
